question: What does the Python quick reference say about mutable and immutable types?
answer: Immutable types are int, float, str, tuple, frozenset, and bool [S1]. Lists, tuples, sets, and dictionaries are discussed in [S3], but the quick reference does not explicitly list them as mutable or immutable [S2]. discusses variables and data types but does not specify mutability for these types.

citations.title: Python Reference Notes
citations.text:
MUTABLE VS IMMUTABLE
Immutable: int, float, str, tuple, frozenset, bool.
Mutable: list, dict, set.
Mutable default arguments are a classic bug; use None as the default value.

citations.text: 4. Lists, Tuples, Sets and Dictionaries A list is an ordered, mutable sequence: nums = [3, 1, 2]. Common methods are append(x) to add at the end, insert(i, x), remove(x), pop() to remove and return the last item, and sort() to sort in place. The built-in sorted(nums) returns a new sorted list and leaves the original unchanged. List comprehensions build lists concisely: [n * n for n in nums if n > 1]. A tuple is an ordered but immutable sequence, written (1, 2). Tuples are used for fixed records and can be dictionary keys because they are hashable. A set stores unique, unordered elements and supports fast membership tests plus union (|), intersection (&) and difference (-). A dictionary maps keys to values: ages = {"Ali": 20, "Mona": 22}. citations.title: Python Lecture Notes
citations.text: 1. Variables and Data Types A variable is a name that refers to a value stored in memory. In Python you create a variable by assignment, for example age = 21. Python is dynamically typed: the type belongs to the value, not to the name, so the same name can later refer to a string. The core built-in types are int (whole numbers), float (decimal numbers), str (text), bool (True or False) and NoneType (the single value None, meaning "no value"). The function type(x) reports the type of x. Conversion functions such as int("42"), float("3.5") and str(10) create new values of another type; int("abc") raises a ValueError. Strings are immutable sequences of characters. Indexing starts at zero, so "python"[0] is "p", and negative indexes count from the end, so "python"[-1] is "n". Slicing "python"[1:4] returns "yth" (start included, stop excluded).

S4.title: Python Lecture Notes
S4.text: 3. Functions A function is a reusable block of code defined with def. Parameters are the names in the definition; arguments are the values supplied in a call. A function returns a value with return; if no return statement runs, the function returns None. Default parameter values, as in def greet(name, greeting="Hello"), let callers omit an argument. Keyword arguments, as in greet(greeting="Hi", name="Sara"), make calls explicit. *args collects extra positional arguments into a tuple, and **kwargs collects extra keyword arguments into a dictionary. Never use a mutable object such as a list as a default value. The default is created once when the function is defined, so def add(x, bucket=[]) shares one list across all calls. The safe pattern is bucket=None followed by if bucket is None: bucket = []. Variables created inside a function are local to it.
